Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed acceptance criteria we discussed for the private (VPC/peering) deployment so we have clear test gates before we move to Dedicated capacity: 

Summary of customer targets (please confirm):
- Sustained ingest: 600 QPS (1k brief spikes)
- Concurrency target: 250 concurrent sessions
- Generation throughput: average 22 tokens/sec per request (long tail up to 600 tokens)
- Latency SLOs (end-to-end from app -> Redwood endpoint -> app): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms for non-streaming; streaming first-byte p95 <= 90ms, per-chunk p95 <= 60ms

Network/path constraints we need from FinCo to validate:
- Preferred: cloud peering (AWS Transit/PrivateLink) OR Direct Connect; fallback VPN (IPSEC) with performance baseline
- Egress: expected NAT/egress IP ranges, any egress filtering or deep packet inspection that could add TLS/TCP handshake overhead
- Internal latency budget: app -> customer edge <= 25ms; customer edge -> Redwood endpoint <= 80ms (this lets us meet the p95 targets once server processing is accounted for)

What we need next (action items):
1) Please attach or share traceroutes / MTRs from your app hosts to the target ip(s) you plan to use (we referenced 34.198.12.45 in the call) — required for preliminary path qualification. (I've attached a template 'redwood_slo_template.xlsx' and a sample trace we saw in the demo: 'network-trace-log-20261207.txt')
2) Confirm expected request size distribution (percent requests that are <64 tokens, 64-256, 256-600+) and average tokens returned per request
3) Any TLS termination in your environment (LT/edge) versus end-to-end TLS between app and Redwood endpoint?
4) Are you planning bidirectional streaming use-cases (continuous audio transcription or partial-response streaming)? If yes, approximate session durations and average bytes/sec per stream

Proposed tests we will run once you provide traces and traffic profile:
- Synthetic QPS ramp to 1.5x target with steady-state latency capture (p50/p95/p99), TCP/TLS handshake characterization, and streaming tail latency tests.
- Packet capture-assisted replay (if you can provide a small sample) to reproduce slow-path anomalies.

Next steps / scheduling: can we lock a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra team on Thursday 2026-12-10 at 10:00 PT? I’ve tentatively proposed a slot on the calendar (link below).

Thanks — Rafael

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming high-level numbers from our side and a couple clarifying Qs: 

Confirmed traffic profile (approx):
- 65% requests <64 tokens
- 30% requests 64-256 tokens
- 5% requests >256 tokens (long-form receipts / dispute narratives)
- Average tokens returned: ~120
- Expected sustained qps: 600; we can tolerate failover to public API for 5% of traffic during peering maintenance windows

Networking: - We prefer cloud peering (AWS Transit Gateway) but will stand up an IPSEC VPN for the initial validation window.
- Egress: we NAT through two public IPs (34.198.12.45, 34.198.12.46) — we'll confirm any upstream filtering with infra.
- TLS: We terminate TLS at our edge LB (ALB) and use mTLS between services internally; for the Redwood endpoint we plan to keep end-to-end TLS (no intermediate TLS termination beyond LB).

Streaming use-case:
- We will use chunked server-side streaming for partial responses in the payments dispute UI. Typical session: 30–90s, average 10kb/sec outbound. We do not plan continuous audio streaming at launch.

Attached: traceroute and mtr output from two app hosts (see network-trace-log-20261207.txt).

Questions for Redwood:
1) Does Redwood support persistent keep-alive pooling for streaming sessions to avoid repeated TLS handshakes?
2) For the streaming chunk p95 target you listed, is that measured from first request byte at our app to the first chunk arriving at the client, or from the Redwood edge to client? (we want to be precise in our test harness)

Will aim to confirm the calendar invite. —Sana

Folks — quick internal note and proposed test plan after reviewing the traces Sana attached.

Observations from trace:
- One of the app hosts shows a small number of 200–400ms hops around the regional transit hop; looks like transient queuing on their side rather than on our edge.
- TLS handshake durations are generally fine (~45–80ms) but we should validate session reuse during pooling.

Proposed validation steps (internal -> customer coordination):
A) Baseline connectivity: run 5-minute steady MTR from 3 app hosts to both NAT IPs and our target endpoint to establish median/variance. Customer to provide two additional hosts if possible.
B) Simulated load: Redwood to run a controlled QPS ramp (100 -> 900) with a mix matching Sana's percentages; capture p50/p95/p99 for both non-streaming and streaming first-byte/continuous-chunk metrics.
C) Streaming stability: create 50 concurrent streaming sessions for 5–10 minutes to observe chunk p95 and reconnect behavior under NAT timeouts.
D) TLS pooling test: validate keep-alive and session reuse by opening 250 concurrent short-lived connections and measuring handshake repeat rate and added latency.

Action items assigned:
- Rafael: confirm test window and calendar invite with FinCo (target: Thu 2026-12-10 10:00 PT)
- Karthik: prepare test harness and load profile; document expected CPU/GPU per load bucket
- Vivek: review streaming buffer behavior and prepare recommended server-side config for low-latency chunking
- Sana / Tom: provide 2 additional app hosts if possible and confirm NAT/egress filtering details

I’ll draft the exact load script and upload to the shared Drive (link to follow).

—Monica
